title: Lower bound of a length given to the nearest 10
source: Theory IGCSE-13.3 Quick check 1 (80 cm to the nearest 10 cm has lower bound 75 cm); book p.410 half-unit rule
stem: A length is \(({n|int})\,\mathrm{cm}\), correct to the nearest \(10\,\mathrm{cm}\). Write down the lower bound, in centimetres.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Half of 10 is 5, so the lower bound is \(({n|int})-5={A|int}\)
steps.note: Subtract half a unit of the given accuracy.

contexts.stem: A measurement of \(({n|int})\,\mathrm{cm}\) is given to the nearest 10 cm. Write down its lower bound.

title: Upper bound of a mass given to the nearest 10
source: Theory IGCSE-13.3 Quick check 2 (200 kg to the nearest 10 kg has upper bound 205 kg); book p.410 half-unit rule
stem: A mass is \(({n|int})\,\mathrm{kg}\), correct to the nearest \(10\,\mathrm{kg}\). Write down the upper bound, in kilograms.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Half of 10 is 5, so the upper bound is \(({n|int})+5={A|int}\)
steps.note: Add half a unit of the given accuracy.

contexts.stem: A mass of \(({n|int})\,\mathrm{kg}\) is given to the nearest 10 kg. Write down its upper bound.

title: Lower bound of a total mass of several bags
source: Theory IGCSE-13.3 Quick check 3 (4 bags of 12 kg to the nearest kilogram have total lower bound 46 kg); book calculated bounds in 13.3
stem: Each of ({k|int}) bags has a mass of \(({m|int})\,\mathrm{kg}\), correct to the nearest kilogram. Find the lower bound of the total mass, in kilograms.

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: The lower bound of one bag is \(({m|int})-0.5={B|num}\,\mathrm{kg}\)
steps.note: Half a kilogram either side of a value given to the nearest kilogram.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The lower bound of the total is \(({k|int})\times({B|num})={A|int}\,\mathrm{kg}\)
steps.note: k is even, so the total is an integer.

contexts.stem: ({k|int}) identical boxes each have mass \(({m|int})\,\mathrm{kg}\), correct to the nearest kilogram. Work out the lower bound of their total mass.

title: Upper bound of a speed from rounded distance and time

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2020), Question 18. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark.

stem:
This question is 0580/22/F/M/20 Question 18, taken from the official QP.

A car travels at a constant speed.
It travels a distance of \(146.2\) m, correct to 1 decimal place.
This takes 7 seconds, correct to the nearest second.

Calculate the upper bound for the speed of the car.

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: The upper bound of the distance is \(146.2+0.05=146.25\) m, and the lower bound of the time is \(7-0.5=6.5\) s.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The upper bound of the speed is \(146.25\div 6.5=22.5\) m/s.
steps.note: MS: 22.5 nfww, 3 marks in total. Official answer: 22.5.
